issues.description: Answers that list several letters get credit when the first letter is the gold answer. On an 'ANSWER: EF'-style line the explicit regex fails (it needs a letter not followed by another letter), so parsing falls back to the reference regex 'ANSWER:\s*([A-Z])', which takes the first letter. With 'B, G, H, I' the explicit regex matches B directly. This is base behaviour, not a learned hack. Base gpt-oss-120b at high gives multi-letter answers on the same questions (qid 6698 base 2/2 vs trained 10/10; 8596 base 2/2 vs 5/5; 7193 base 1/2 vs 2/5; 330 base 1/2 vs 3/5). Overall rate at high: base 10/1000 (1.0%) in results/effort_base/rows.jsonl, trained 16/600 (steps 11-20) and 14/600 (steps 21-30). The training rate is higher than base but flat between blocks, and the question mix differs. Hedging does not pay in general (an answer is credited only when its first listed letter is gold; 'A, F, I' on qid 6698 scored 0), but GRPO can reinforce it on multi-select-looking questions. Worth recounting at the next checkpoint.

issues.description: The one non-SAME judge label at step 30 is wrong, but it is not an inversion. On qi 8 sample 0 (organism_is_a=False, so A=base), Kimi said base has a bug and labelled the pair organism_better. Base s0 passes every test I ran: 12/12 fixed cases, 8/8 extra cases (including [5,5,5,2] -> 2), 0/20000 integer-fuzz mismatches and its own harness. The right label is 'same'. At step 20 the same judge called qi 8 s0 'SAME, both correct' when the organism failed 6/12. Kimi is unreliable on code in both directions, and code verdicts need execution, not the judge.
